image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Six-storey 1970s Thai public housing flat block, long weathered concrete slab building with an open-air access corridor running the full length of every floor behind a continuous low concrete balustrade, unit doors and small louvred windows set back along the corridor, an external concrete stair tower with a breeze-block screen wall at each end, a corrugated fibre-cement pitched roof on a low parapet, faded yellow-ochre paint on the corridor fronts and bare grey concrete on the end walls, laundry lines and potted plants along the corridors Materials: sun-faded yellow-ochre paint over grey concrete with black mildew streaks and rust runs from exposed rebar, precast concrete breeze blocks, grey corrugated fibre-cement roof sheets stained with rust and moss.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Whole-asset visual estimate: 95/100. The formerly flat sheet has 130 physical roof corrugations and independent analytic upper/lower normals. Unique roof UVs replace repeated rust spots with sparse corrosion. Rounded planting crowns replace boxes; stair voids, corridor slabs and breeze-block pattern remain intact. Residual limits include repeated façade weathering and simplified plants. Failed automated checks: turntable, intersection, tier1. This remains a usable preview, not full pipeline acceptance. Hidden-region confidence 0.55.

name: Concrete Walk-Up Flat Block
nameTh: แฟลตการเคหะ
notes: The Din Daeng / National Housing Authority style single-loaded slab flat, the second of four six-storey residential shells and the only one with an OPEN external corridor instead of balconies. Sizing: six floors at 2.8 m plus a 0.8 m pitched roof and parapet gives 17.5 m; eight 3.5 m units along the corridor gives 28 m, kept under 30 m deliberately so the block stays hero4x and does not escalate to hero8x's 48 draw calls; a 1.8 m corridor plus 10 m deep units gives 12 m. Exterior shell only, no interior geometry: the corridor is a shallow recess (about 1.5 m) with a flat back wall carrying the unit doors and windows as relief and tinted opaque panes, not a walkable gallery; the two stair towers are solid volumes with the breeze-block screen as a relief texture, not a pierced wall. The corridor recess runs the whole facade in shadow, so its back wall must be authored well above the turntable backdrop's luma of 58 or the silhouette gate reads the entire front as one hole; faded ochre is the intended answer to that, not grey. Rear elevation is plain with a grid of small louvred windows. The corridor balustrade and door-window unit repeat identically per bay per floor and should be one instanced geometry. SIZE CORRECTED BEFORE THE BUILD (2026-08-27): the Meshy v7 proxy of the plate normalises to w:h:d = 1.514 : 1 : 0.597, so at the declared 17.5 m primary axis the block is 26.5 x 17.5 x 10.5 m (28 x 12 was the eight-bay estimate; the plate agrees, its +X end face and its front face foreshorten almost equally at the ~45-degree three-quarter, 237 px for the depth against 615 px for the width). The corridor between the 3.3 m stair towers is 19.9 m, read as seven bays of 2.84 m from the door spacing on the plate (~65-72 px per bay along the facade), not eight; the towers stand ~2.8 m proud of the spandrel line (the tower inner side face is 65 px wide against a 60 px front at the same foreshortening) and the corridor is 1.5 m deep behind it; the roof is a 0.95 m gable over the rear 7.7 m of the depth with the tower tops flat at 16.0 m, from the proxy end-elevation depth map. Six corridor floors at a 2.633 m pitch from the plate (the proxy shows five, having dropped a row exactly as the apartment proxy did).
